protocol.instrument_name: Medicines, Poisons and Therapeutic Goods (Pharmacist Extended Scope of Practice- Urinary Tract Infection) Authorisation 2025 (No 1)
protocol.effective_date: Signed 30 October 2025 by Dr Kerryn Coleman, Chief Health Officer; "This instrument commences the day after notification." (section 2, page 1)
protocol.legal_basis: made under the Medicines, Poisons and Therapeutic Goods Regulation 2008, Section 490A, Authorisations for health practitioners to deal with medicines with CHO approval—Act, s 20 (1) (c) (page 1). Schedule 1: "made under section 490A of the Medicines, Poisons and Therapeutic Goods Regulation 2008 for the purposes of establishing conditions and criteria under which a registered pharmacist may initiate the supply of the particular medicine or class of medicine to which the authorisation relates in the absence of a supply authority (prescription)." (page 2)
protocol.supervision_model: "A registered pharmacist# may deal with a medicine or a class of medicine to which the authorisation relates to under their own authority (without a prescription) to a person under the following conditions" (Schedule 1, page 2): the medicine is listed under Part A – Medicines Authorisations; the patient is eligible under the patient eligibility criteria under Part A; any other Part A conditions; Part B – Pharmacist Training Requirements met; "The patient and the pharmacist must both be physically present at a pharmacy that meets the listed requirements of Part C – Premises Standard, for consultation with the patient to occur prior to supply"; Part D – Record Keeping Requirements met; pharmacists follow the approved clinical protocols under Part E; comply with AHPRA and Pharmacy Board of Australia Code of Conduct (breaches handled under Part F – Governance and Complaints). # "A Pharmacist is a person who holds registration under the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law (ACT) and is employed or engaged in a pharmacy that meets the requirements in Part C."
protocol.scope_summary: ACT notifiable instrument NI2025–612 authorising a registered pharmacist to supply a medicine or class of medicines without a prescription for urinary tract infection when the supply is performed in accordance with the ACT Pharmacist Extended Scope of Practice Urinary Tract Infection Authorisation (Schedule 1). Approved medicines (Part A i): nitrofurantoin, fosfomycin, trimethoprim, cefalexin in a strict hierarchical order. Eligible patients: people assigned female at birth aged 18 to 65 years, assessed against the Appendix 1 UTI Clinical Protocol flowchart (adapted from the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Use of Antibiotics to Treat Urinary Tract Infection, used in the ACT with permission). Conditions cover training (Part B), premises (Part C), record keeping and seven-year retention plus record sharing (Part D), clinical protocols (Part E) and governance/complaints (Part F). Document is current as issued (No 1, 30 October 2025); it contains no repeal wording.

inclusion.text: Person who is assigned female at birth
Patient has two or more of the above symptoms; Symptoms of uncomplicated UTI include dysuria, urinary frequency, urinary urgency, and/or suprapubic pain or discomfort.

exclusion.text: Systemic symptoms suggesting: Pyelonephritis (including fever >38°C, chills, nausea, malaise, and/or flank pain), or

Recurrent UTI (2 or more within 6 months or 3 or more within 12 months)
Symptoms of UTI persisting 48-72 hours after starting appropriate antibiotic treatment
Symptoms of UTI reoccur within 2 weeks after finishing appropriate antibiotic treatment
Visible haematuria (blood in urine)
Pyuria (pus in urine)
Renal disease, impaired renal function and history of renal stones
Catheterisation
Previous episodes of pyelonephritis
Immunocompromised or taking immunosuppressant medicines (e.g., azathioprine, cyclosporin, cyclophosphamide, methotrexate [including low dose])
History of blood disorder/porphyria
Spinal cord injury
Diabetes
Recent insertion of IUD within the last 3 months
Resident of a residential aged care facility (RACF)

Patient has only one of the above symptoms (one symptom is not sufficient to indicate presence of a UTI)

diagnosis_pathways.name: UTI Clinical Protocol (Appendix 1) eligibility, diagnosis and treatment flowchart

steps.description: Flowchart entry gate: "Person who is assigned female at birth". Yes -> continue. No -> "Not eligible for antibiotic supply. Provide non-pharmacological advice and direct patient to seek medical advice from a general practitioner."

gates.criterion: Person who is assigned female at birth

steps.description: Gate: "Aged 18-65 years". Yes -> continue. No -> "Not eligible for antibiotic supply. Provide non-pharmacological advice and direct patient to seek medical advice from a general practitioner."

Gate: "Systemic symptoms suggesting: Pyelonephritis (including fever >38°C, chills, nausea, malaise, and/or flank pain), or Suspected sepsis (including fever, difficulty breathing, fast heart rate, low blood pressure and mental confusion)." Yes -> "Not eligible for antibiotic supply. Direct patient to attend emergency department immediately." No -> continue.

gates.criterion: Systemic symptoms suggesting pyelonephritis or suspected sepsis

steps.description: Gate: "Patient has symptoms or contraindications including: Pregnancy or 4-6 weeks post-partum; Recurrent UTI (2 or more within 6 months or 3 or more within 12 months); Symptoms of UTI persisting 48-72 hours after starting appropriate antibiotic treatment; Symptoms of UTI reoccur within 2 weeks after finishing appropriate antibiotic treatment; Visible haematuria (blood in urine); Pyuria (pus in urine); Renal disease, impaired renal function and history of renal stones; Catheterisation; Previous episodes of pyelonephritis; Immunocompromised or taking immunosuppressant medicines (e.g., azathioprine, cyclosporin, cyclophosphamide, methotrexate [including low dose]); History of blood disorder/porphyria; Spinal cord injury; Diabetes; Recent insertion of IUD within the last 3 months; Resident of a residential aged care facility (RACF); Medical or surgical gender affirming care that impacts urinary tract function". Yes -> "Direct patient to seek medical advice from GP. Only conservative management with non-prescription medicines (if appropriate) and self-care advice may be provided by pharmacist". No -> continue.

gates.criterion: Patient has symptoms or contraindications (any of the 16 listed conditions)

steps.description: Gate: "Symptoms or medical history suggest a cause other than acute UTI (such as vaginal thrush or irritation)." Yes -> "Treatment and/or referral to GP based on presenting symptoms." No -> continue.

gates.criterion: Symptoms or medical history suggest a cause other than acute UTI (such as vaginal thrush or irritation)

steps.description: Gate: "Symptoms or risk factors including: Multidrug-resistance bacteria-risk factors including: Recent (within the previous 3 months) or frequent treatment with antibiotics; Recent (within the previous 3 months), frequent or long-term resident of a healthcare facility, history of being hospitalised in the last 4 weeks; Overseas travel within the previous 3 months, or overseas travel within previous 6 months to regions with high prevalence of antimicrobial resistance (e.g., South Asia, South-East Asia) particularly if the patient has received medical care or treatment with antibiotics in that region; Infection with multidrug-resistant bacteria within the previous 3 months. Risk factors for sexually transmissible infection, defined as: Age < 29 years or previous STI, or Sexual contact without a condom/dental dam outside a mutually monogamous relationship, a new sexual partner in last 60 days, a sex partner recently treated for an STI, sexual contact with a sex worker. Currently taking medicines that increase the risk of UTI, such as sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors. Intrauterine device (IUD) in situ (for more than 3 months)." Yes -> "Treat using conservative measures or antibiotic treatment, if clinically appropriate. Refer the patient to a GP for review after provision of treatment by the pharmacist." No -> continue (continued next page).

gates.criterion: Symptoms or risk factors (multidrug-resistance risk factors, STI risk factors, SGLT2 inhibitors, or IUD in situ for more than 3 months)

steps.description: "Symptoms of uncomplicated UTI include dysuria, urinary frequency, urinary urgency, and/or suprapubic pain or discomfort." Gate: "Patient has two or more of the above symptoms". Yes -> provisional diagnosis (PW-1-S9). No -> see PW-1-S8.

gates.criterion: Patient has two or more of the above symptoms

steps.description: Branch for "Patient has only one of the above symptoms (one symptom is not sufficient to indicate presence of a UTI)" (Yes) -> "Not eligible for antibiotic supply. Provide conservative treatment only. Direct patient to attend seek medical advice if symptoms progress."

"Provisional diagnosis of uncomplicated UTI can be made. Consultation must then include: Obtain informed consent from the patient for: participation, financial consent and pharmacist communication with other health practitioners. Document evidence of consent made by the pharmacist in the patient's clinical record."

"Initial therapy: review the Therapeutic Guidelines approach to management of acute cystitis. As per the Therapeutic Guidelines, discuss option of nonantibiotic therapy (analgesia with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs [NSAIDs]). Explain benefits and risks to types of therapy. Note patients on non-antibiotic therapy are less likely to need antibiotics; however, without antibiotics, 1-5% are expected to progress to pyelonephritis or sepsis."

"Provide education on non-pharmacological management and self-care including symptom management and when to seek medical care: Educate patients prone to developing UTIs about prophylaxis; Urinary alkalising agents: efficacy of these agents for the symptomatic treatment of UTI have not been established however some patients find them useful. These agents significantly reduce the antimicrobial effect of nitrofurantoin."

"If empirical antibiotic therapy is recommended with an Approved Medicine, check first that the patient does not have any allergies or contraindications (refer to medical practitioner for treatment if so): First Line: Nitrofurantoin 100mg orally, every 6 hours for 5 days, or Second Line: Fosfomycin 3g orally, as a single dose, or Third Line: Trimethoprim 300mg orally, daily at night for 3 nights. If nitrofurantoin, fosfomycin or trimethoprim cannot be used for empirical therapy for acute cystitis in nonpregnant adult females, use: Cefalexin 500mg orally, every 12 hours for 5 days. Note: the hierarchical order above must be followed for all consultations. Where a patient has a My Health Record, the pharmacist must ensure the details of supply are uploaded to My Health Record, unless requested otherwise by the patient. Always consider drug allergies and interactions when selecting treatment."

gates.criterion: Patient does not have any allergies or contraindications to the selected Approved Medicine

steps.description: "Provide follow-up advice and expectations about symptom resolution:" Advise the patient that symptoms should respond to appropriate antibiotic treatment within 48 hours; advise the patient to seek medical care if symptoms worsen (e.g. fever 38°C or higher, rigors, loin or back pain, vomiting) or do not improve within 48 hours; advise on what to do if side effects of medication occur; Review the Therapeutic Guidelines indications for urinalysis; advise the patient to seek care from a GP if symptoms reoccur within 2 weeks after finishing antibiotic treatment, or symptoms develop that are not symptoms of an acute UTI; where patient has a regular GP or general practice service share a record of the consultation, within a week, with the patient's consent.

"Where GP referral or follow-up is required but the patient does not have a regular GP or that GP is unavailable (within an appropriate timeframe), contact Healthdirect on 1800 022 222 for advice on patient disposition."

treatments.quantity_to_supply: Pharmacists must not supply a medicine in a quantity that exceeds the duration of treatment specified in Part E. If the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack of a medicine exceeds the quantity listed in Part E, the pharmacist may supply the medicine in the smallest available size, but for no longer than 12 weeks.

open_questions.observed: In the plain-text conversion the Appendix 1 flowchart boxes on pages 7 and 8 are interleaved/garbled (adjacent and rotated boxes read character-by-character). The wording transcribed here was read from rendered page images of the same PDF file; all page numbers still come from the === PAGE n === markers.
open_questions.why_unclear: Extraction artefact of the flowchart layout, not ambiguity in the document itself.

open_questions.topic: Flowchart connector between 'cause other than acute UTI' outcome and the risk-factor node
open_questions.observed: The outcome box "Treatment and/or referral to GP based on presenting symptoms." has an arrow that appears to point down-left into the following "Symptoms or risk factors including:" node, while the same node is also reached by the "No" branch.
open_questions.why_unclear: Direction/meaning of the connector is ambiguous in the diagram; it is unclear whether assessment continues after treatment/referral to GP.

open_questions.topic: Risk-factor node outcome permits treatment (recorded as red flags, not exclusions)
open_questions.observed: The Yes branch of "Symptoms or risk factors including:" reads "Treat using conservative measures or antibiotic treatment, if clinically appropriate. Refer the patient to a GP for review after provision of treatment by the pharmacist." - i.e. supply is still permitted.
open_questions.why_unclear: The document does not state whether patients in this branch remain eligible for antibiotic supply, so these items are captured as red flags (REVIEW_GP) rather than as eligibility exclusions.

open_questions.observed: Pyelonephritis is defined as "fever >38°C" (page 7) while follow-up advice says "fever 38°C or higher" (page 8). Both readings are recorded (RF-1 operator '>' and RF-29 operator '>='); they are not reconciled.
open_questions.why_unclear: Contradictory thresholds (>38 vs >=38) printed in two places of the same flowchart.

open_questions.topic: Adverse event report body printed as 'Therapeutic Goods Association'
open_questions.observed: Part A iii (page 4) reads "this must be reported to the Therapeutic Goods Association ... by reporting online at https://aems.tga.gov.au/". The AEMS portal is operated by the Therapeutic Goods Administration.
open_questions.why_unclear: Name as printed may be a typographical error; transcribed verbatim without correction.

open_questions.topic: Criteria combinatorics not stated in prose
open_questions.observed: The Appendix 1 flowchart uses sequential Yes/No gates; no AND/OR combinatorics are stated in the prose of Part A or Schedule 1.
open_questions.why_unclear: Inclusion criteria are combined with all_of (every gate must pass) and each exclusion bullet group with any_of (any one bullet diverts the patient), inferred from the diagram structure.

open_questions.topic: Not-eligible outcome wording for single-symptom branch
open_questions.observed: Text layer of the outcome box reads "Not eligible for antibiotic supply. Provide conservative treatment only. Direct patient to attend seek medical advice if symptoms progress."; the rendered box visually ends at "if symptoms" (possible clipping) and the wording "attend seek medical advice" is unusual.
open_questions.why_unclear: Visible render appears clipped/overlapping; full sentence taken from the PDF text layer.

open_questions.topic: No branch shown for a patient with none of the listed UTI symptoms
open_questions.observed: "Patient has only one of the above symptoms (one symptom is not sufficient to indicate presence of a UTI)" has a Yes branch to the not-eligible outcome box but no visible No branch on page 8.
open_questions.why_unclear: The pathway for a patient with none of dysuria/frequency/urgency/suprapubic pain is not shown in the diagram.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Part B permits "Any other Accredited training advised or required by the Chief Health Officer" in addition to the PSA Managing Uncomplicated Cystitis / Australasian College of Pharmacy Uncomplicated Cystitis Treatment courses - confirm which additional accredited training is accepted before go-live.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Open-ended training category delegated to the Chief Health Officer; not enumerated in the instrument.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Follow-up requires pharmacists to "Review the Therapeutic Guidelines indications for urinalysis" and to review "the Therapeutic Guidelines approach to management of acute cystitis" - confirm the Therapeutic Guidelines edition/subscription available at go-live.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: External clinical reference is required but the exact edition/section is not specified in the instrument.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Supply-quantity rule: "If the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack of a medicine exceeds the quantity listed in Part E, the pharmacist may supply the medicine in the smallest available size, but for no longer than 12 weeks" - confirm the local supply-quantity procedure for each approved medicine before go-live.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Quantity supplied depends on local pack sizes and a 12-week cap left to pharmacy operations; no numeric quantities are printed.

hugh_to_confirm.item: "Where a patient has a My Health Record, the pharmacist must ensure the details of supply are uploaded to My Health Record, unless requested otherwise by the patient" - confirm the local process/system integration for My Health Record uploads before go-live.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Operational requirement dependent on local pharmacy software configuration.
